27.note: This project has enough surviving documentation to support a fuller case study. The sections below describe documented responsibilities, technologies and visible interface behavior; they do not claim formal UX research that is not recorded.

ux.title: Responsive conference information with a dynamic agenda
ux.intro: The strongest UX/UI evidence in the surviving TCT 2014 material is the way a large conference information set was organized across desktop, tablet and mobile, including a dynamic agenda rather than a static schedule.

panels.title: Information structure
panels.copy: Conference content, schedules and industry information had to remain understandable across multiple related web experiences. The documented work includes TCT and TCT Industry interfaces, responsive layouts and agenda views.

panels.title: Interaction + data
panels.copy: The dynamic agenda used interactive transitions and asynchronously loaded content connected to the same data source used by the conference app, giving the website and app a shared information foundation.

16.note: This project has enough surviving technical detail to show a focused UI/front-end case study. The presentation stays with documented implementation and interaction work rather than adding unrecorded research claims.

ux.title: Interaction design expressed through front-end behavior
ux.intro: Dallas Leipzig is useful as a UI case study because the surviving record identifies specific interface behaviors rather than only a finished website image.

panels.title: Interface states
panels.copy: The work included animated transitions between sliders, collapsing elements and active interface states, requiring the interaction behavior to remain clear as content changed.

panels.title: Responsive implementation
panels.copy: The interface was implemented across a responsive PHP/SCSS/JavaScript environment using AngularJS, jQuery and Bootstrap.

5.note: This project supports a full design-system/campaign case study because the surviving portfolio documents the identity across print, email, web graphics, production and fulfillment.

ux.title: One event identity across many user touchpoints
ux.intro: The design problem was larger than a single invitation. Guests encountered event information through invitation components, response materials, hotel and directions information, email and supporting event pieces.

panels.title: Information hierarchy
panels.copy: The invitation, RSVP, dinner selection, hotel information and directions each carried different information while remaining visibly part of the same event package.

panels.title: System consistency
panels.copy: The Gatsby-inspired identity was extended across print, email, website graphics, sponsorship and event materials instead of redesigning every touchpoint independently.

workflow.title: Event identity
workflow.copy: Establish the Gatsby-inspired visual language, typography and recurring graphic details.

workflow.label: 02 · EXTEND
workflow.title: Invitation suite
workflow.copy: Apply the system to the invitation, belly band and seal, RSVP, dinner selection, hotel and directions information.

workflow.label: 03 · CAMPAIGN
workflow.title: Digital + event
workflow.copy: Extend the same identity to programmed email, website graphics, sponsorship pieces and supporting event materials.

workflow.label: 04 · PRODUCE
workflow.title: Physical fulfillment
workflow.copy: Prepare production files, print, assemble invitations, wrap bands, prepare envelopes and mail the completed package.

1.note: This project supports a focused editorial/design-system case study. It has strong publication evidence but less surviving process documentation than the larger campaign and development projects.

ux.title: A repeatable editorial system for print and digital viewing
ux.intro: The useful design evidence is the recurring page structure: content needed to read coherently in print while also working as a digital flip-book publication.

panels.title: Editorial hierarchy
panels.copy: Feature pages and recurring layouts organized school, family and education content into a consistent reading system.

panels.title: Cross-format consistency
panels.copy: The same publication identity and layout logic supported both printed distribution and digital flip-book viewing.

deliverables.title: Publication design
deliverables.copy: Visual system and editorial page layouts for the Fall 2019 issue.
